creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 9, item 4.

`clamp(val, min, max) -> error|int|float` fails only when `min > max`, which is known statically when both bounds are literals. `--strict` still flags it:

```rad
f = clamp(0.4, 0.0, 1.0)
```

```
warning[RAD30011]: This call can fail; the error isn't handled and would halt the script
```

In a repo that keeps `--strict` clean so the fallible calls that matter stand out, the reporter replaced it with a nested ternary, which is longer and hides what the line does. Same class as the done card a_25Nhy9Un4 (hints on provably-safe code). Narrowing on literal bounds fixes this one; worth sweeping the other math builtins with error-only-on-bad-literal-args for the same shape.

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1).

Where: rts/check/type_check.go, refineBuiltinReturn.
title: clamp() with literal bounds trips RAD30011 under --strict
